evals.prompt: Add a background step to the project module that fills Project.tier from each organization's plan. Call it backfill_project_tier.
evals.expected_output: Renames the id to `project:<kebab-name>` (for example project:fill-project-tier): defineMigrationStep throws migration_step_declaration_refused with malformed_id for that shape, and collection refuses a foreign prefix (foreign_prefix) or a repeated id (duplicate_id). Declares kind data, mode background, a one-line operator-facing description, needsOldWritersGone: true if an old image still writes projects without a tier. The run body is a thin call into a service in services/ using the binder's repositories and peer *Api (dependencies), saves checkpoint.save({ report }) after each committed batch, reads checkpoint.resumeFrom, stops on signal.aborted and writes nothing (not even a checkpoint) on dryRun.

evals.prompt: The next release can't work until this backfill finishes, so make it blocking. It uses ProjectService and the Prisma client to compute the values.
evals.expected_output: A blocking step is frozen SQL: it runs at its own release's schema during a jump, when the newest Prisma client names columns that may not exist yet. So it imports no service, no peer *Api and no typed client; it reaches tables only through the owner's prisma.<subject>-migration.repository.ts with raw SQL naming every column (exemplar prisma.ops-migration.repository.ts, called by ops:copy-automation-migration-state). It may touch only tables created in its own release and never a sign-in or ingest table. If the logic needs ProjectService, it stays background, and the release must tolerate it being unfinished. Only kind data may be blocking (blocking_not_data).

evals.prompt: Write the unit test for my new migration step. Calling run once and checking the rows were updated is enough, right?
evals.expected_output: No. Over the module's memory twins, call the declared step's run with a test checkpoint ({ resumeFrom, save }) and an AbortSignal, and prove: twice is once (the second run reports nothing to do), dry run writes no row and saves no checkpoint, resume from a saved report continues after it, an old writer after the run is caught up by a re-run (level-triggered), and the source is intact (copy, never move). An installation test asserts the steps collect (migrationStepsOf). Never calls the upgrade runner from a unit test.

evals.prompt: Our new peer projection in trace folds annotation events. Add a note to the release docs asking operators to run a projection replay after deploy.
evals.expected_output: No operator replay: declares defineProjectionReplayStep in the owning module's .withMigrations, taking `replayer` from the binder (({ replayer }) => [...], never built by the module), with id <module>:<kebab-name>, a description, lane set to the projection's lane constant, and needsOldWritersGone: true because an old worker does not know the new lane. Optional since narrows a handed-over fold to the deploy overlap. It is a data step in background mode; the report carries replayedThrough so a reopened run only refolds aggregates touched after it. Exemplars: scim:replay-sso-connection-view (trailingPass) and governance:replay-cost-charges (bounded since).

evals.prompt: We need to move each organization's files to the new storage layout, keeping the old path readable until each one is verified. Run it at startup so it's done before anyone uses it.
evals.expected_output: This is a tenant step: defineMigrationStep with kind tenant, mode background, tenants set to the axis, title, the rollout flags and migrateTenant (not a SystemMigration class answered through registeredMigrations(), which is transitional), never run at startup. The framework keeps per-tenant state; the upgrade asks a worker for a pass. migrateTenant is re-runnable and self-proving (finalized when the proof passes, migrated and held when it disagrees, parked when work may have committed without its follow-up), declares candidateTenants so a pass walks only tenants with work, copies rather than moves, and awaits waitForRoom between pages of commands so the pass paces by its own queue work. A provider choice by an operator is a named task outside the ledger (plan, copy, finalize, verify), as object-storage-migrate.task.ts.

evals.prompt: Backfill needs three kinds of events per project row. I planned three steps, one per event, each walking the project table.
evals.expected_output: One pass per table (Alex, 2026-10-12): one step walks the table once and records every event it needs for each row, in pages with sendBatch and stable per-row keys, saving the checkpoint after each page so the step paces by its own queue work. Prerequisite ordering is kept (after), shipped step ids are not renamed or removed. The events go to every projection, subscriber and process manager like any other; a backfilled field is data a consumer may read, never routing.
